rows.title: Four Terms You'll Use All Unit

notes.prompt: Matter: anything that has _______ and takes up ________.
Pure substance: ___________ of particle throughout. ________ composition.
Mixture: two or more substances _____________ combined. Composition ___________.
Solution: a ______________ mixture, evenly mixed, same throughout.

notes: *Ask two questions: can it be separated physically, and are the parts evenly mixed.

rows.title: Element, Compound, Molecule

notes.prompt: Element: one kind of _______ only. Cannot be broken down _____________.
Compound: two or more ___________ bonded in a ______________.

notes: *O₂ is a molecule but not a compound. Compound needs two different elements.

rows.title: Evenly Mixed, or Not

notes.prompt: Homogeneous = ___________. Same throughout. You _________ see the parts.
Heterogeneous: parts stay ___________. You ______ see them.

notes: *If a scoop from the top matches a scoop from the bottom, it is homogeneous.

rows.title: Run Six Samples Through the Chart
cues: Separated physically first, then evenly mixed.
notes: *O₂ is an element, not a compound. Steel is a solution too.

conceptReview.title: Unit 1 / Concept Review
conceptReview.subtitle: Connect the ideas, check common mix-ups, and explain the science in your own words.

sections.heading: Classifying matter
paragraphs: **Matter** has mass and occupies space. A **pure substance** has a fixed composition;
a **mixture** has variable composition and can be separated by physical means.

left.heading: Pure substances
lines: chemically bonded in a fixed ratio.

right.heading: Mixtures
lines: also called a solution (such as salt water).

sections.watchOut: O₂ is a molecule and an element. CO₂ is a molecule and a compound.

sections.heading: Reading an atom or ion
paragraphs: **Proton:** +1 charge, about 1 amu, in the nucleus.
**Neutron:** 0 charge, about 1 amu, in the nucleus.
**Electron:** −1 charge, very small mass, outside the nucleus.
**Z = protons.** This determines the element. **A = protons + neutrons.**
Neutrons = A − Z. Neutral atoms have equal numbers of protons and electrons.
Positive ions have lost electrons; negative ions have gained electrons.
sections.watchOut: Forming an ion changes electrons, not the element’s proton count.

sections.heading: Understanding average atomic mass
paragraphs: **Isotopes:** atoms of the same element with the same protons but different neutrons.
**Abundance:** the fraction or percentage of atoms that are a particular isotope.
**Weighted average:** each isotope’s mass contributes according to its abundance.
**Calculate:** Convert each percent to a decimal. Multiply each isotope’s mass by its abundance as a decimal, then add the products. Report the result in amu.
**Check:** The average falls between the isotope masses, closer to the more abundant one.
sections.watchOut: 75.76% = 0.7576. Mass number is a count; average atomic mass is weighted.

quickRecall: Why is O₂ an element even though it contains two atoms?
What changes when an atom becomes an ion? What changes between isotopes?
Why is chlorine’s average atomic mass closer to 35 than to 37?
